title: ASA Physical Status Classification
sources: ASA Physical Status Classification System (2020 update)
purpose: Universal shorthand for baseline perioperative risk; drives every anesthesia plan. Append "E" for emergency procedures.

tiers.label: ASA I
tiers.description: A normal healthy patient (non-smoker, no or minimal alcohol use)

tiers.label: ASA II
tiers.description: Mild systemic disease without substantive functional limitation (e.g. current smoker, well-controlled HTN or DM, obesity 30 ≤ BMI < 40, pregnancy)

tiers.label: ASA III
tiers.description: Severe systemic disease with substantive functional limitation (e.g. poorly controlled DM/HTN, COPD, BMI ≥ 40, active hepatitis, pacemaker, ESRD on dialysis, MI/CVA/TIA > 3 months ago)

tiers.label: ASA IV
tiers.description: Severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life (e.g. recent < 3 months MI/CVA/TIA, ongoing cardiac ischemia, severe valve dysfunction, sepsis, DIC, ESRD not on scheduled dialysis)

tiers.label: ASA V
tiers.description: A moribund patient not expected to survive without the operation (e.g. ruptured AAA, massive trauma, intracranial bleed with mass effect)

tiers.label: ASA VI
tiers.description: A declared brain-dead patient whose organs are being removed for donation

interpretation.label: Assign the class from overall systemic disease burden and functional status
interpretation.detail: The classification is a subjective clinical assessment, not a point score. Add "E" (e.g. ASA IIIE) for emergency cases.
